summary: The PR fails to implement half of the issue (Wikipedia links with parentheses) and places URL parsing/punctuation logic in the generic HTML renderer instead of the URL plugin.
checked: uv run python -c 'import mistune; md = mistune.create_markdown(plugins=["url"]); print(repr(md("see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details")))'
uv run python -c 'import mistune; md = mistune.create_markdown(plugins=["url"]); print(repr(md("did you try https://example.com/docs?")))'

findings.problem: Pull request completely fails to address part 1 of the issue: Wikipedia links with parentheses get cut off.
findings.evidence:
uv run python -c 'import mistune; md = mistune.create_markdown(plugins=["url"]); print(repr(md("see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details")))' -> '

see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) for details

\n'
findings.suggestion: Update the URL plugin pattern and parser to properly handle balanced parentheses in URLs (such as Wikipedia links) as well as trailing punctuation.

findings.problem: Trailing punctuation trimming is placed in `HtmlRenderer.link` rather than the `url` plugin, causing it to apply globally to all standard Markdown links (`[text](url)`) rather than just raw auto-linked URLs.
findings.suggestion: Move URL cleaning and punctuation/parentheses adjustment logic into `src/mistune/plugins/url.py` (`URL_LINK_PATTERN` and `parse_url_link`).
